headline: Broad Rally Takes Shape as Homebuilders Lead and Iran Risk Rattles Energy Markets
body_html:
Wednesday's mid-session picture is one of sturdy, if uneven, advance. With 412 names moving higher against 138 in retreat across our 550-name universe, buyers hold a commanding edge. Homebuilders are pacing all sectors with a gain of roughly 4%, anchored by a surge of more than 6% in Toll Brothers, while Healthcare adds nearly 2% and Materials climbs 1.68%. The tape is broad, and the risk-on tone is unmistakable — even as geopolitical unease over the Strait of Hormuz keeps traders one headline away from a mood shift.

The session's most arresting single-stock move belongs to Estée Lauder, up more than 15% and running well clear of the pack. Merck follows with a gain approaching 10%, lending particular strength to the pharma sub-sector. Marvell Technology has surged more than 8%, a conspicuous outlier in Semiconductors — the only sector in negative territory, off 0.79% — where Tokyo Electron and MaxLinear are both under meaningful pressure.

Into the close, traders will be watching Hormuz shipping-lane updates closely; oil hit a three-week high on supply uncertainty, and any escalation language from Tehran or its neighbors could reprice energy and risk assets rapidly. Bond yields are edging lower despite the geopolitical backdrop, a signal worth monitoring as the afternoon session develops.

briefs.headline: Estée Lauder Surges More Than 15%, Leads Universe
briefs.body: Shares of Estée Lauder are the session's standout mover, vaulting more than 15% and sitting at the top of the leaderboard across our 550-name coverage universe. The consumer-beauty name is attracting outsized volume, and the move is lifting sentiment across the broader consumer sector, which is up 1.62% on the day.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Uncertainty Pushes Oil to Three-Week Peak
briefs.body: Crude prices have climbed to their highest level in three weeks as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows amid persistent uncertainty about the waterway's status. The UAE's financial embargo on Iran, imposed following a missile threat, has sharpened the regional rivalry and injected a fresh risk premium into energy markets mid-session.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Bucks the Rally, Slides 0.79%
briefs.body: While the broader market advances, Semiconductors are the lone sector in the red, dropping 0.79% as mid-session trading progresses. Tokyo Electron has shed nearly 10%, MaxLinear is off more than 4%, and Amkor Technology is down roughly 3.5%, pointing to specific supply-chain and equipment concerns weighing on the group.

briefs.headline: La-Z-Boy Drops Nearly 12%, Sharpest Decliner on the Day
briefs.body: La-Z-Boy is the session's worst-performing name, falling 11.49% and standing out even against a backdrop of broadly rising equities. The furniture maker's sharp slide is dragging on consumer-discretionary sub-sector sentiment and has drawn attention from desk traders monitoring divergences within an otherwise constructive consumer tape.

briefs.headline: France Moves to Expel Iranian Diplomats as Tensions Escalate
briefs.body: France's foreign minister announced that two Iranian diplomats will be expelled in the coming days, adding a European dimension to the widening diplomatic confrontation with Tehran. The move follows the expiration of a US-Iran ceasefire and comes as South Korea's government warned that Washington appears to be applying pressure on Seoul regarding its posture toward Iran.

briefs.headline: Merck Climbs Nearly 10%, Anchors Healthcare Advance
briefs.body: Merck is posting a gain of nearly 10% in mid-session trading, providing a powerful lift to the Healthcare sector's 1.99% advance. Sarepta Therapeutics is also contributing, rising 6.85% in the biotech sub-sector. Together, the two names are helping make Healthcare one of the session's clearest areas of institutional interest.
